proof.text: The smoothness hypotheses give the indicated relative dimensions for the structure maps (the pure-codimension convention gives $d_j-c_j$ for $Z_j$). By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), base change preserves these dimensions and by clause (2) the products $P=U_1\times_kU_2$ and $Q=Z_1\times_kZ_2$ are smooth over $k$, so the frame-class definition applies to $h$. On affine charts of $U_1$ and $U_2$, if the frame ideals are $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_{c_1})$ and $J=(g_1,\ldots,g_{c_2})$, the product ideal of $Q$ in $P$ is $I\otimes_k\mathcal O_{U_2}+\mathcal O_{U_1}\otimes_kJ$. Thus it is generated by the entries of $h=(p_1^*f_1,\ldots,p_1^*f_{c_1},p_2^*g_1,\ldots,p_2^*g_{c_2})$, and its scheme-theoretic zero locus is $Q$. The empty-tuple case is the unit support convention.

source.place: Step 5, first sentence: product frame on U_1\times_k U_2

proof.text: Write $\alpha_i=\partial\kappa(f_i|_{U_1\setminus V(f_i)})$ and $\beta_j=\partial\kappa(g_j|_{U_2\setminus V(g_j)})$. The pullback and boundary clauses of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] give $p_1^*\alpha_i=\partial\kappa(p_1^*f_i)$ and $p_2^*\beta_j=\partial\kappa(p_2^*g_j)$, with the corresponding pulled-back supports. Therefore the factors defining $\operatorname{cl}(h)$ are exactly the pullbacks of the factors defining $\operatorname{cl}(f)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(g)$.

source.place: Step 5, naturality of the frame factors under the two projections

proof.text: Write $\alpha'_i=p_1^*\alpha_i$ and $\beta'_j=p_2^*\beta_j$. By [def-pur-frame-class], $\operatorname{cl}(h)$ is the left-associated supported cup product $\alpha'_1\cup\cdots\cup\alpha'_{c_1}\cup\beta'_1\cup\cdots\cup\beta'_{c_2}$ in this order. The pullback clause of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] gives $p_1^*\operatorname{cl}(f)=\alpha'_1\cup\cdots\cup\alpha'_{c_1}$ and $p_2^*\operatorname{cl}(g)=\beta'_1\cup\cdots\cup\beta'_{c_2}$, with supports $Z_1\times_kU_2$ and $U_1\times_kZ_2$, whose scheme-theoretic intersection is $Q$ (Step 1). Associativity from the same lemma regroups the concatenated product as $(\alpha'_1\cup\cdots\cup\alpha'_{c_1})\cup(\beta'_1\cup\cdots\cup\beta'_{c_2})$; the order of the factors is unchanged, so no sign occurs. The twist multiplication identifies the coefficient $A(c_1)\otimes_AA(c_2)$ with $A(c_1+c_2)$, compatibly with the left-associated coefficient $A(1)^{\otimes_A(c_1+c_2)}$ of [def-pur-frame-class] by associativity of the sheaf tensor. Hence $\operatorname{cl}(h)=p_1^*\operatorname{cl}(f)\cup p_2^*\operatorname{cl}(g)$ in $H^{2(c_1+c_2)}_Q(P,A(c_1+c_2))$ for the cup product of [def-pur-supported-cup]. If $c_1=0$ or $c_2=0$ the corresponding factor is the unit $1$, and $\gamma\cup1=\gamma$ because the coefficient map of [def-pur-supported-cup] sends $\overline1\otimes\overline1$ to $\overline1$.

source.place: Step 5, equality by naturality and associativity of supported cup products

proof.text: Coefficient comparison. Put $Z'_1=Z_1\times_kU_2$, $Z'_2=U_1\times_kZ_2$, with closed immersions $i'_1,i'_2$, and let $\xi_1:p_1^{-1}C_{Z_1}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{Z'_1}(A)$, $\xi_2:p_2^{-1}C_{Z_2}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{Z'_2}(A)$ be the closed-immersion exchanges of [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback], where $C_D(A)=(D\hookrightarrow T)_*A_D$. Each exchange is the mate of the unit, so by the triangle identity $\xi_r\circ p_r^{-1}(q_{Z_r})=q_{Z'_r}$ under $p_r^{-1}A=A_P$; here $q$ is the constant restriction (adjunction unit), the quotient map of [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product]. Let $\theta:C_Q(A)\to p_1^{-1}C_{Z_1}(A)\otimes_Ap_2^{-1}C_{Z_2}(A)$ be the comparison of [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product] for $M=N=A$, and $\mu:C_{Z'_1}(A)\otimes_AC_{Z'_2}(A)\to C_Q(A)$ the coefficient multiplication of [def-pur-supported-cup]. By their defining formulas, $\theta q_Q(1)=p_1^{-1}q_{Z_1}(1)\otimes p_2^{-1}q_{Z_2}(1)$ and $\mu(q_{Z'_1}(1)\otimes q_{Z'_2}(1))=q_Q(1)$. Hence $\mu(\xi_1\otimes\xi_2)\theta q_Q=q_Q$; since $q_Q:A_P\to C_Q(A)$ is epic and an $A_P$-linear map out of $A_P$ is fixed by the image of $1$, $\theta=(\xi_1\otimes\xi_2)^{-1}\mu^{-1}$. The modules are flat in degree zero ([def-pur-supported-cup]), so the derived comparisons $\theta^L$ and the $\theta$ of [def-pur-supported-cup] are these underived maps.

source.place: Step 5, final sentence: identification with the specified exterior product (coefficient maps)

proof.text:
Classes. Let $a=2c_1$, $b=2c_2$, $F=A(c_1)_{U_1}$, $G=A(c_2)_{U_2}$, $x=\operatorname{cl}(f)$, $y=\operatorname{cl}(g)$; the pro-etale twists are the comparison inverse images of the etale ones by the twist identification of [sk-def-purity-conv]. Write $\chi$ for the identification of [lem-pur-supported-hom]. By [lem-pur-supported-hom-adjunction-transpose] (for $U_1,U_2,P$ of finite type over $k$, hence locally Noetherian), $\chi(x)=x^\flat[a]$, $\chi(y)=y^\flat[b]$, and a class $z$ on $P$ with support $Q$ is determined by $\chi(z)=z^\flat[a+b]$. The class $\operatorname{cl}(f)\boxtimes\operatorname{cl}(g)=\kappa^{Z_1,Z_2}_{F,G}(x\otimes y)$ of [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product] has adjoint $(p_1^{-1}\epsilon\otimes p_2^{-1}\epsilon)\theta^LC_Q(x\otimes y)=(p_1^{-1}x^\flat\otimes p_2^{-1}y^\flat)\theta$, by naturality of $\theta^L$ and the counit formula for adjoints. By [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] (pro-etale clause), $\chi(p_r^*x)=p_r^{-1}\chi(x)\circ\xi_r^{-1}$. Thus by [def-pur-supported-cup] and Step 4,
$$\chi(p_1^*x\cup p_2^*y)=\sigma_{a,b}\bigl(p_1^{-1}x^\flat[a]\otimes p_2^{-1}y^\flat[b]\bigr)(\xi_1\otimes\xi_2)^{-1}\mu^{-1}=\sigma_{a,b}\bigl(p_1^{-1}x^\flat[a]\otimes p_2^{-1}y^\flat[b]\bigr)\theta.$$
Since $a,b$ are even, $\sigma_{a,b}$ and the identification $A[-a]\otimes_AA[-b]=A[-a-b]$ carry no signs, so this is $\chi(\kappa(x\otimes y))$, both read in $p_1^{-1}F\otimes_A^Lp_2^{-1}G$ and then in $A(c_1+c_2)$ by the same twist multiplication. Hence $p_1^*\operatorname{cl}(f)\cup p_2^*\operatorname{cl}(g)=\operatorname{cl}(f)\boxtimes\operatorname{cl}(g)$; with Step 3 this proves the statement, the empty tuples giving units on both sides.

title: Exterior product of frame classes
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient datum $k,\ell,E,n,\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ of [sk-def-purity-conv]. For $j=1,2$, let $U_j$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] separated finite-type $k$-scheme of constant dimension $d_j$, let $Z_j\hookrightarrow U_j$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z_j$ smooth of pure codimension $c_j\geq0$, and let $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_{c_1})$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_{c_2})$ be tuples of global functions generating the respective ideal sheaves. Their frame classes $\operatorname{cl}(f)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(g)$ mean the supported Kummer-boundary products of [def-pur-frame-class]. Put $P=U_1\times_kU_2$, $Q=Z_1\times_kZ_2$, with projections $p_j$, and assume $Q$ has pure codimension $c_1+c_2$ in $P$. The concatenated tuple $h=(p_1^*f_1,\ldots,p_1^*f_{c_1},p_2^*g_1,\ldots,p_2^*g_{c_2})$ generates the ideal of $Q$. With the canonical twist identifications, one has
$$\operatorname{cl}(h)=p_1^*\operatorname{cl}(f)\cup p_2^*\operatorname{cl}(g)=\operatorname{cl}(f)\boxtimes\operatorname{cl}(g)\quad\text{in }H^{2(c_1+c_2)}_Q(P,\Lambda(c_1+c_2)).$$
The middle cup product uses the pulled-back supports $Z_1\times U_2$ and $U_1\times Z_2$ and the specified supported coefficient multiplication [def-pur-supported-cup]; the last term is the class induced by the specified pro-etale supported exterior-product map [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product]. Empty tuples use the unit class. No independence of frames, gluing, or comparison with smooth purity is asserted.
